articles.title: Former Giants coach defends star player Malik Nabers against character questions from broadcast analyst
articles.summary: Wink Martindale says someone may have put criticism in Greg Olsen's ear about Malik Nabers, suggesting motives tied to the Giants star's contract.
articles.body: When his character came into question, Giants star wideout Malik Nabers took to social media to take on former player and TV analyst Greg Olsen, who criticized the receiver’s sideline demeanor during Sunday's broadcast. One former New York Giants coach is running to Nabers' defense. Ex-Giants defensive coordinator Wink Martindale, who had a messy split with the team in 2024, harbors no bad blood toward the receiver and spoke up to defend Nabers against Olsen's critique. "I'm with Malik on this. Somebody put that in his ear, whether it's to keep his contract down for the next year when they want to extend him or whatever it is, I don't know. But just keep playing," Martindale said, appearing on Giants insider Pat Leonard's "Talkin' Ball" podcast. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "I love the kid. I love his competitiveness." During the Giants' visit to Philadelphia on Sunday, Olsen and boothmate Joe Davis kept pointing to Nabers' "negative" body language on the sideline. They also called him out for pouting after a Giants drive finished with an Isaiah Likely touchdown. "His body language has been terrible today," Davis said. KANSAS CITY CHIEFS STAR DEFENSIVE LINEMAN CHRIS JONES CAUGHT IN SCREAMING MATCH WITH COACHES ON SIDELINES Olsen proved more frustrated with Nabers. "I have played with a lot of really good wide receivers, a lot [of] really good players. There's never been a great wide receiver who hasn't demanded the ball. That kind of comes with the territory. But there is a very fine line between being demanding, being a competitor, and all those great things. That's great. It just can never cross that it feels like it takes away from the success of your teammates. MALIK NABERS REVEALS HOW GIANTS COACH JOHN HARBAUGH HELPED HIM OVERCOME HIS ACL INJURY FEARS "So when your teammate catches a wide-open touchdown, you need to be the happiest guy on the field. You can't still be worried about your targets. That's the fine line. He is a talented, young, really good player. You've just got to keep it in check." Martindale added, "Think about all the great players that John Harbaugh's coached. Does he get blown up more because it's in New York? Of course it does. But it's nothing new for John." Martindale knows a thing or two about friction inside New York's building. Following months of simmering tension during the 2023 season, his Giants tenure imploded in January 2024 after head coach Brian Daboll fired Martindale’s trusted defensive assistants. Martindale reportedly cursed out Daboll, stormed out, and mutually parted ways. Despite showing visible frustration during the Giants' 19-11 win in Philadelphia, where he had five catches for 43 yards after four straight 100-yard games, Nabers' commitment was never questioned by his locker room. Giants players publicly defended him as a "good teammate, " with running back Cam Skattebo noting that Nabers' sideline annoyance when lacking targets simply reflects a competitive edge teammates "love to see." articles.title: Daniel Jones 'Not Happy' Colts Traded Keenan Allen, Josh Downs and More In NFL Deadline Fire Sale
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts are going to look much different when they take the field for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins than they did at the start of the season after a number of trades, and quarterback Daniel Jones isn't thrilled about the situation.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are going to look much different when they take the field for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins than they did at the start of the season after a number of trades, and quarterback Daniel Jones isn't thrilled about the situation.

"I mean, honestly, you're not not happy to see it, right?" Jones told reporters (h/t Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk). "You're a player and you're going out there competing and doing everything you can to win games. So you're not happy to see a lot of those decisions, and—but like I said, it's outside of our control, and our job is to play, be prepared, and play well. So, like I said, we got a lot of trust in the guys coming into those spots, and we'll be ready to go."

Indianapolis traded wide receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, as well as defensive lineman DeForest Buckner and offensive lineman Quenton Nelson. Allen and Downs were two of Jones' top targets in the aerial attack, while Nelson was a key part in the protection up front.

Yet the Colts didn't end up trading running back Jonathan Taylor despite plenty of speculation they would, so Jones can at least still rely on his backfield mate and one of the best playmakers in the league to help lead the offense.

It has been a season to forget in Indianapolis, as it fell to 2-7 with Sunday's loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

Jones has struggled as well with six touchdown passes to 10 interceptions after largely playing well last season with 19 touchdown passes to just eight interceptions.

Losing the team's best offensive lineman and two of its top wide receivers won't make life easier for Jones, so it would be anything but a surprise if he continues to struggle from a statistical standpoint.

The Colts are in rebuilding mode at this point, but the immediate future doesn't look great for the quarterback or his teammates.

articles.title: Rams star Puka Nacua out for an 'extended period' after suffering injury on final play of win
articles.summary: Puka Nacua sprained his MCL and PCL and sustained turf toe, and Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay said he will be out for an extended period of time.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Rams will be without their top wide receiver for an extended period. Puka Nacua sprained his MCL and PCL and sustained a turf toe injury during the Rams' 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders on Sunday. He will be sidelined for an extended period, coach Sean McVay said Wednesday. "We won’t place him on IR due to some semantics with the roster and things like that, but he’ll be out for an extended period of time," McVay said, according to The Athletic. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Although Nacua missed two games earlier this season due to injury, he has been incredibly productive when healthy. In seven games, the two-time Pro Bowler has 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns. Compounding the Rams' problems, they are now without their top two wide receivers, as Davante Adams remains sidelined with a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 6. The Rams play the Green Bay Packers in Week 12 on Thanksgiving Eve, and McVay said the team is currently targeting that crucial NFC matchup for Adams' return. They hope Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith can step up in their absence while also leaning on their deep group of tight ends. articles.title: “Just adore him and I think he is the greatest”: How Jason and Travis Kelce turned two Chiefs fans' unusual requests into special memories with heartfelt gestures
articles.summary: An autograph from an NFL star can become a lifelong memory. For two Kansas City Chiefs fans, that memory came in an unusual way.
articles.body: An autograph from an NFL star can become a lifelong memory. For two Kansas City Chiefs fans, that memory came in an unusual way. Jason and Travis Kelce each signed a fan's prosthetic leg during separate Chiefs games, turning two unexpected requests into memorable moments. While Jason's interaction happened in October 2024, Travis followed a year later, giving another supporter a reason to remember her night at Arrowhead Stadium.The two incidents also showed a different side of the Kelce brothers. Beyond their NFL achievements, both took time to connect with supporters who wanted something more personal than a photograph or a signed football.Jason Kelce and the ESPN crew answered Samantha Secord's unusual requestThe first incident took place on October 7, 2024, when the Chiefs hosted the New Orleans Saints on Monday Night Football. Samantha Secord, a Chiefs season-ticket holder from Omaha, travelled more than 184 miles to watch her team. This time, she had a special request: she wanted Jason Kelce to sign her prosthetic leg.Secord and her friends tried to get the ESPN crew's attention during the broadcast. Their efforts eventually worked when Scott Van Pelt noticed them and helped bring the leg to the crew. Jason and the other ESPN personalities signed it during a commercial break.Speaking to KCTV5 on October 10, 2024, Secord described the experience as "kind of mind-blowing." However, she still had one autograph in mind."My favorite player is Travis Kelce. I just adore him, and I think he is the greatest," she told KCTV5. "He is the one that I am absolutely looking forward to signing my leg."Her request carried a personal meaning. Secord lost her leg after a 2022 UTV accident that injured the lower half of her body. She also explained that watching Travis play and following his community work helped her during recovery. Travis Kelce signed another fan's prosthetic leg after reaching 100 touchdownsA year later, on October 27, 2025, Travis had his own memorable interaction with a Chiefs supporter. Kansas City defeated the Washington Commanders 28-7, and Kelce reached 100 career touchdown receptions, becoming only the fourth tight end in NFL history to achieve the milestone.After the game, a different female fan caught his attention by raising her prosthetic leg towards him. People around her helped pass it to the tight end, who signed it as the crowd cheered. ESPN shared the interaction on its TikTok page.The gesture came during a night when Kelce had plenty of reasons to celebrate. Speaking to Scott Van Pelt during ESPN's postgame interview, he joked about his longevity."I'm just the old lucky dog that's still able to do this thing," Kelce said.Patrick Mahomes also praised his longtime teammate after the victory, calling him the "true Chiefs Chief." Head coach Andy Reid highlighted Kelce's energy and continued contribution to Kansas City.The two incidents involved different fans, but they shared a similar moment of connection. Jason and Travis each took time to fulfil an unusual autograph request, giving two Chiefs supporters memories that went far beyond the game.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Titans' Calvin Ridley gives his side of Nashville airport 'incident' with valet, awaits possible charges
articles.summary: Calvin Ridley said he took his keys from a Nashville airport valet's hand during a late-night dispute over a missing ticket, and the valet claimed a broken finger.
articles.body: Calvin Ridley, the veteran Tennessee Titans wide receiver, gave his side of an "incident" that occurred at Nashville International Airport this past weekend. Ridley acknowledged his involvement in the incident confirmed by the Titans, describing it as a back-and-forth argument with an airport valet while trying to retrieve the keys to his truck. Speaking with reporters, Ridley said he took his keys from the valet’s hands when he didn’t have the ticket needed to retrieve them, though he said he showed other documents proving the truck was his. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "I took my keys out of his hand," Ridley said, via Yahoo Sports. "I didn't have the ticket. Once you don't have the ticket, you show him your ID, you fill out a form. I also showed him a picture, I also showed him more that it's my truck. "My wife and kids was at the top. My mom was at the top. I came down by myself to get it. It's 11 p.m. at night. They gave me the hardest time to get my truck. I just got my keys, got the registration. "They wanted the registration. I gave them the registration after I got the keys. My wife came down. We got in the truck and left." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Ridley added the valet suffered an injury to one of his fingers. He was asked about the nature of the injury, but Ridley said, "I don’t know what I did. I didn’t look at nothing." "He yelled I broke his finger," Ridley said. "I don’t know what happened." Titans head coach Robert Saleh categorized the incident as "a very minor miscommunication." Ridley said he has yet to hear from law enforcement, but a report from A to Z Sports on Monday stated the valet wants to press charges. It remains unclear as of Wednesday if charges have been filed. The report also cited sources that said Ridley was frustrated when the valet wouldn’t give him his keys. Ridley also confirmed the report stating he didn’t have his ticket and the valet couldn’t verify his truck. The reason for the reporter asking Ridley on Wednesday if the valet’s finger was cut was due to the report stating "one of the keys (or something on the keychain) cut the valet’s hand in the process" of him trying to take his keys. Ridley was expected to be a potential NFL trade candidate, as the Titans sit at 1-7 entering Week 10 in yet another struggling season. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ wife Brittany Mahomes shares a heartwarming glimpse of motherhood after announcing her fourth pregnancy
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ top quarterback, and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, have been perfect parents to their three children, Sterling,
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ top quarterback, and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, have been perfect parents to their three children, Sterling, Bronze and Golden Raye, as they are all set to welcome their fourth into the world. As the star player prepares for the clash against the Atlanta Falcons, Patrick Mahomes’ wife, Brittany Mahomes, has made a new update after their pregnancy reveal.Patrick Mahomes’ wife Brittany Mahomes, shares a new update with her children as the star player remains focused on the fieldA few hours ago, Patrick Mahomes’ wife Brittany Mahomes, took to her social media to share a heartwarming clip with her children. The video shows Brittany Mahomes in their children's game room as she spins them around.The clip starts with Golden Rayte speaking cutely to the camera as her mother stands behind her and grabs her legs to spin her around. Brittany Mahomes then repeats the same with their son, Bronze, and oldest daughter, Sterling as the children keep giggling.The text on the video reads as, “Spinning trend with our kids” while the caption read as, “This was fun😂🥹🤍”.While the top quarterback Patrick Mahomes has not commented on the video yet, his mother Randi Mahomes wrote, “"Priceless giggles 😍😍”.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes have remained dedicated parents to their three children as they gear up for their fourth.While the three time Super Bowl Most Valuable Player has remained busy on the field, his wife Brittany Mahomes has been balancing being there for their children.Patrick Mahomes remains busy as Brittany Mahomes takes up the responsibility to be present for their childrenOver the last few years, Patrick Mahomes’ wife Brittany Mahomes has gone public with how each pregnancy, things have been difficult for her. But fortunately, the Kansas City Current co-owner has bounced back well from each of her pregnancies as she even showed up to be there for her husband, just days after giving birth to their youngest child last year.The Kansas City Chiefs’ top quarterback Patrick Mahomes has often spoken about how he prefers spending more and more time with his children so that he does not miss out on their growing years.A few weeks ago, in an interview with PEOPLE, Patrick Mahomes reflected on his life as he said, “Football is a huge part of my life, but I’ve always tried to keep perspective…Family, friends, my teammates, my foundation work, those things have always been important to me.”He adds, “During the season you’re so locked in, so having that time to slow down, be present with the kids, and just enjoy the people around you makes it special.”For now, all eyes remain on the popular quarterback as he gears up to face the Atlanta Falcons.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Struggling Colts QB Daniel Jones admits he's 'not happy' watching Indy's front office strip away teammates
articles.summary: Daniel Jones admitted he's frustrated after the Colts dealt Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Keenan Allen, and Josh Downs in a two-week sell-off.
articles.body: The captain of the sinking 2-7 Colts ship is not happy. Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones admitted he is frustrated watching the front office gut his supporting cast. Before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline passed, acting GM Ed Dodds traded away guard Quenton Nelson, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs over two weeks. Jones, 29, made his displeasure clear when facing reporters on Wednesday. "I mean, honestly, you’re not happy to see it, right?" Jones said. "You’re a player, and you’re going out there competing and doing everything you can to win games. So you’re not happy to see a lot of those decisions, but like I said, it’s outside of our control, and our job is to play, be prepared, and play well. So, like I said, we got a lot of trust in the guys coming in to those spots, and we’ll be ready to go." Jones is stuck throwing to backups, though his own play led to the teardown. Had DJ delivered, Indy would be buying instead of selling. Through nine games, the $88 million quarterback has six touchdown passes, 10 interceptions and a dismal 68.9 passer rating. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Meanwhile, ex-Colts celebrated getting out. Former Indy wideout Josh Downs posted a Vince Carter tears-of-joy GIF on X right after his Tuesday trade to Kansas City. "It's great to join a team like this with so much history, so much winning, in their past and even now," Downs told reporters on his first day with KC. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Indy's biggest miss was reportedly rejecting a second- and fifth-round offer from the Giants for running back Jonathan Taylor, then stalling on a trade offer for Grover Stewart until the suitor pulled out. With their 2027 first-round pick already owed to the Jets from the Sauce Gardner trade, the Colts' front office needed to stockpile draft picks. Holding onto Jones, Taylor, and Stewart turns the rest of this season into pointless mileage on veterans who should have fetched picks. articles.title: Broncos' deal for Chargers LB Daiyan Henley falls through after NFL trade deadline
articles.summary: No reason was provided for the trade getting spiked.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos appeared to fill an immediate need with a trade for Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley. That deal is no longer happening.

Denver announced in a statement late Wednesday night that the deal, which would have seen the Chargers receive a 2027 fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick , was no longer happening. No reason was provided.

"The proposed trade involving Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley will not be finalized. We have great respect for Daiyan as a player and person, and we wish him all the best moving forward."

The development means Henley will remain with the Chargers, the only winless team in the NFL at 0-8. The deal was going to be a rental for the Broncos as Henley is a pending free agent, but the former third-round draft pick will now spend the remainder of the final year of his rookie contract in Los Angeles.

Henley has a salary of $3.7 million this season, per OverTheCap .

The Broncos, who have won five straight games, approached Tuesday's trade deadline in need of additional depth at linebacker and appeared to get that in the 27-year-old Henley, who leads the Chargers with 51 combined tackles as well as two passes defended, a forced fumble, an interception and a half sack in eight games this season.

Denver's defense ranks 10th in points allowed and 26th in total yards, while also playing more snaps than any unit in the NFL at 648. Veteran inside linebacker Alex Singleton has played 647 of those, making him the most-used defensive player in the league, and fellow inside linebacker Justin Strnad isn't far behind him at 529 snaps.

Henley would have helped give that pair some rest as a rotational option, but the Broncos will have to figure that situation out without the help of the trade deadline.
